373	// or null value returns "" like an absent field so the existing
374	// missing-endpoint checks report it; a present non-string value keeps the
375	// edges type error; an unpaired surrogate fails the import, naming the
376	// endpoint it came from and quoting the original escape.
377	func unmarshalEndpointName(raw json.RawMessage, endpoint string) (string, error) {
378		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
379		if trimmed == "" || trimmed == "null" {
380			return "", nil
381		}
382		name, badEscape, ok := decodeLineageName(raw)
383		if !ok {
384			return "", errInvalid(`lineage document edges must be an array of {"from": ..., "to": ...} objects: ` +
385				`endpoint "` + endpoint + `" must be a JSON string`)
386		}
387		if badEscape != "" {
388			return "", errInvalid(`lineage document edge "` + endpoint + `" endpoint contains an ` +
389				"unpaired Unicode surrogate escape '" + badEscape +
390				"'; surrogate escapes are valid only as a matched " +
391				`\uXXXX\uYYYY high-low pair`)

396	// objectFrame tracks one container during the structural key scan: whether it
397	// is an object (arrays need no key tracking), whether the next string token is
398	// that object's key, and the keys already seen in it.
399	type objectFrame struct {
400		object    bool
401		expectKey bool
402		keys      map[string]bool
403	}
404	
405	// rejectDuplicateKeys tokenizes the text and rejects any JSON object that
406	// repeats a key, any document whose top-level value is not an object, and any
407	// trailing JSON value after the closing object. encoding/json accepts all
408	// three silently (last key wins; null decodes into a map as no value at all;
409	// trailing values are rejected by Unmarshal but with a generic message), so
410	// the explicit scan makes document problems deterministic.
411	func rejectDuplicateKeys(text string) error {
412		dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(text))
413		// Numbers are only structure here, never values: keep them as raw
414		// json.Number literals so a syntactically valid number of any magnitude
415		// (1e400, a hundred-digit integer) tokenizes without a float64 range
416		// error. The scanner still validates the literal itself, so 01, 1e or
417		// NaN remain malformed JSON and fail the document.
418		dec.UseNumber()
419		var stack []objectFrame
420		rootClosed := false
421		for {
422			tok, err := dec.Token()
423			if err == io.EOF {
424				if len(stack) != 0 || !rootClosed {
425					return errInvalid("lineage document must be one complete JSON object")
426				}
427				return nil
428			}
429			// Anything at all after the root object closes is a second value or
430			// garbage, whether tokenized as a token or as a scan error.
431			if rootClosed {
432				return errInvalid("lineage document must hold exactly one JSON object")
433			}
434			if err != nil {
435				return errInvalid("lineage document must be one complete JSON object: " + err.Error())
436			}
437	
438			switch t := tok.(type) {
439			case json.Delim:
440				switch t {
441				case '{':
442					stack = append(stack, objectFrame{object: true, expectKey: true, keys: map[string]bool{}})
443				case '[':
444					if len(stack) == 0 {
445						return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays, got an array")
446					}
447					stack = append(stack, objectFrame{})
448				case '}', ']':
449					if len(stack) == 0 {
450						return errInvalid("lineage document has an unmatched " + string(t))
451					}
452					stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
453					if len(stack) == 0 {
454						if t != '}' {
455							return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays")
456						}
457						rootClosed = true
458					} else if stack[len(stack)-1].object {
459						// A nested container was this object member's value; the
460						// next member, if any, starts with a key.
461						stack[len(stack)-1].expectKey = true
462					}
463				}
464			case string:
465				if len(stack) == 0 {
466					return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays, got a string")
467				}
468				top := &stack[len(stack)-1]
469				if !top.object {
470					continue // string element of an array; members are delimiter-tracked
471				}
472				if !top.expectKey {
473					top.expectKey = true // string value consumed; a key may follow
474					continue
475				}
476				if top.keys[t] {
477					return errInvalid("lineage document contains a duplicated object key: " + t)
478				}
479				top.keys[t] = true
480				top.expectKey = false
481			default: // number, bool, nil
482				if len(stack) == 0 {
483					return errInvalid("lineage document must be a JSON object with nodes and edges arrays")
484				}
485				if stack[len(stack)-1].object {
486					stack[len(stack)-1].expectKey = true
487				}
488			}
489		}
490	}

492	// findLineageCycle returns the datasets on one directed cycle written in the
493	// actual derivation direction (upstream -> derived), with the smallest-named
494	// dataset on the cycle first and repeated last, or nil when the graph is
495	// acyclic. Every node on a cycle reaches itself by following parent edges, so
496	// a depth-first walk with a per-path stack catches a back edge of any length,
497	// including a self dependency. Nodes are visited in Go string order and parent
498	// lists are already sorted, so the reported cycle is independent of the
499	// document's node and edge ordering.
500	func findLineageCycle(graph map[string]*Lineage) []string {
501		color := make(map[string]int, len(graph)) // 0 unseen, 1 on current path, 2 done
502		var stack []string
503		var found []string
504	
505		var visit func(node string) bool
506		visit = func(node string) bool {
507			color[node] = 1
508			stack = append(stack, node)
509			for _, parent := range graph[node].Parents {
510				switch color[parent] {
511				case 0:
512					if visit(parent) {
513						return true
514					}
515				case 1:
516					// A back edge to a node on the current path closes a cycle:
517					// parent ... node, with node deriving from parent.
518					start := 0
519					for stack[start] != parent {
520						start++
521					}
522					found = append([]string(nil), stack[start:]...)
523					return true
524				}
525			}
526			stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
527			color[node] = 2
528			return false
529		}
530	
531		names := make([]string, 0, len(graph))
532		for name := range graph {
533			names = append(names, name)
534		}
535		sort.Strings(names)
536		for _, name := range names {
537			if color[name] == 0 && visit(name) {
538				return derivationCycle(found)
539			}
540		}
541		return nil
542	}
543	
544	// derivationCycle converts a closed cycle segment discovered while following
545	// parent edges into the derivation direction, then rotates it so the
546	// smallest-named dataset comes first (and stays last). A parent-direction
547	// segment [p0, p1, ..., pk] closes with pk deriving from p0, so the derivation
548	// runs p0 -> pk -> ... -> p1 -> p0.
549	func derivationCycle(parentPath []string) []string {
550		body := make([]string, 0, len(parentPath)+1)
551		body = append(body, parentPath[0])
552		for i := len(parentPath) - 1; i >= 1; i-- {
553			body = append(body, parentPath[i])
554		}
555	
556		min := 0
557		for i := 1; i < len(body); i++ {
558			if body[i] < body[min] {
559				min = i
560			}
561		}
562		rotated := make([]string, 0, len(body)+1)
563		rotated = append(rotated, body[min:]...)
564		rotated = append(rotated, body[:min]...)
565		rotated = append(rotated, body[min])
566		return rotated
567	}
